requirements.requirement: Existing data under /srv/inventory owned by user inventorysvc
requirements.summary: inventorysvc system user was created (cmd-e203cb594fbc46fa) and chown -R inventorysvc:inventory-readers applied (cmd-40117f36ef3a4dca). Post-repair ls -la confirms inventorysvc as owner on the directory tree and both files, and this ownership is unchanged after the node restart (cmd-8181bdb0897944ab, cmd-94940462b3b1441b).

Group inventory-readers created (cmd-d667b307f4e3466c) and applied as group owner; directories set to 750 and files to 640 (cmd-40117f36ef3a4dca). A temporary user placed in inventory-readers successfully read records.csv (cmd-3bee9a4a24354fb3), then was removed (cmd-3ffc42b0f60c4952), directly demonstrating group readability.

requirements.requirement: Data inaccessible to other (non-owner, non-group) users
requirements.summary: With directories at 750 and files at 640, the unrelated user antrieb received 'Permission denied' attempting to list and read the tree (cmd-a9c8546968884596), directly confirming other users are blocked.

requirements.requirement: Existing file contents preserved (byte-for-byte) through the repair
requirements.summary: sha256sum of config.json and records.csv taken before repair (cmd-836d3b0fe8c344be) matches checksums taken immediately after the chown/chmod (cmd-ab442599eda84b55) and again after the later restart (cmd-94940462b3b1441b); all three show identical hashes matching the prepare-stage baseline.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence: /srv/inventory is owned by inventorysvc:inventory-readers, permissions are 750/640 giving group members read access while blocking other users (demonstrated via a positive group-member read test and a denied unrelated-user access test), and file contents are proven byte-identical to the pre-repair baseline via matching checksums taken before, immediately after, and following the node restart. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also executed cleanly: pre-restart boot_id and healthy state were captured, the reboot acknowledgement returned before disconnection, a different post-restart boot_id was observed, and all required state (user, group, ownership, permissions, checksums) was confirmed recovered — consistent with the fixed after-prepare/after-executor boot-identity snapshots.
limitations: Package-health checks were unavailable (timed out) at every lifecycle stage, so it cannot be confirmed the restart or repair left package state undamaged, though no other evidence suggests it did.
SELinux context of the files/directories was not explicitly re-verified after chown/chmod, though this was not part of the stated task contract.

operational_hygiene.summary: State-changing commands are all traceable to the task: several early groupadd/useradd attempts failed due to PATH/permission issues (cmd-54948a6724314ef4, cmd-8443bfa00127471e, cmd-0cb31cea003d4479) without mutating state, before the executor found working invocations (cmd-d667b307f4e3466c, cmd-e203cb594fbc46fa). The temporary tmpreader account created to verify group read access (cmd-3bee9a4a24354fb3) was deleted immediately afterward (cmd-3ffc42b0f60c4952), a bounded and fully reverted verification step. The mandatory restart protocol (cmd-0ec6b903dec74d24) left a small /tmp/reboot.log artifact as an incidental byproduct of the reboot command's own output redirection, visible in the after_executor snapshot; this is low-risk residue directly tied to the required restart evidence collection rather than an unnecessary mutation.
